title: USB camera setup and HPS-only live classification
update:
Live classification on the DE1-SoC (updated Nov 22, 2026)

The USB camera connects to the HPS USB host. Linux captures MJPEG frames through V4L2 and decodes them to RGB on the HPS. The board also preprocesses each frame and prints the predicted ImageNet class in its Linux terminal. PuTTY on Windows displays that terminal. The linked recording shows the earlier CPU-only demo that used Windows preprocessing.

Image preprocessing
- Resize the shorter side to 256 pixels using bicubic interpolation, preserving aspect ratio. Take a 224 × 224 center crop.
- Scale RGB values to [0, 1], subtract the channel means (0.485, 0.456, 0.406), and divide by the channel standard deviations (0.229, 0.224, 0.225). Supply the resulting FP32 tensor in channel-first order.

TinyViT-5M versus TinyViT-21M accuracy on HPS
- Tested both FP32 MNN models with two HPS CPU threads and zero FPGA jobs. Both received identical preprocessed tensors for 200 saved Imagenette validation images, 20 per class, and predicted across all 1,000 ImageNet classes.
- TinyViT-5M: 158/200 top-1 (79.0%) and 195/200 top-5 (97.5%).
- TinyViT-21M: 167/200 top-1 (83.5%) and 199/200 top-5 (99.5%).
- On this subset, 21M made nine more correct first-choice predictions overall, gaining 4.5 percentage points in top-1 and 2.0 points in top-5 accuracy.

The live 21M hybrid demo also ran on the board with HPS-local capture and preprocessing. Each classified frame reported 207 FPGA jobs, two offloaded linear layers and one resident MLP pair. A remaining measurement goal is to separate capture, preprocessing, transfer, inference and display time under matched conditions.
